messages:
Maya: customer reports streaming responses cut off mid-stream, client gets ECONNRESET and they see the call counted as a 5xx on their invoice. request_id=rc-9f3b2a, region=us-west1, customer app uses fetch() with ReadableStream.
Devon: can you paste a minimal repro? also which client lib/version? sometimes old proxies mishandle chunked responses.
Maya: repro attached from customer: curl with --no-buffer to keep streaming:
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-customer" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -d "{\"model\":\"redwood/xx-1\",\"input\":\"ping\"}" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream
```
Maya: client logs show: "read ECONNRESET" right after a final chunk arrives; server side shows 200 then an upstream proxy log entry with status 502; billing pipeline flagged it as a user-visible 5xx.
Keiko: tagging infra, can we check gateway logs for rc-9f3b2a and TCP half-close events? may be nginx proxy sending FIN before body full drained.
ops-bot: alert: gateway-us-west1 stream-error-rate spike at 14:02 UTC (+18%): traces: https://kibana.redwood.internal/app/discover#rc-9f3b2a
Devon: I'm seeing a pattern where client FIN (RST) occurs but our billing aggregator treats any upstream error after downstream FIN as a 5xx. we should distinguish client-abort scenarios.
Raj: quick check: in the gateway logs rc-9f3b2a shows upstream_response_time=2.4s, bytes_sent=10240, proxy_status=UPSTREAM_RESET, downstream_status=200, remote_addr=203.0.113.45. the kernel shows a TCP FIN from client at 14:02:10.
Maya: customer insists they didn't cancel — their app retries and the second attempt succeeds. they care because they're charged and their metrics show high 5xx.
Devon: can you run this grep to pull the raw proxy frames?
```
sudo rg "rc-9f3b2a" /var/log/gateway/* | sed -n '1,200p'
```
Keiko: done, pasted snippet: "PROXY_FRAME: chunked: 1->0 body-trailer-present=false upstream: -> FIN because peer reset" — looks like upstream closed due to idle keepalive reaper on the edge router.
Raj: hypothesis: edge router has aggressive idle timeout for connections with long-lived streaming; it injects a FIN, client sees ECONNRESET, we count a 5xx because upstream reported reset.
Maya: customer uses single long-stream session (~90s). they say this started after a cloud provider network change last week.
Devon: temporary mitigation: set shorter server-side keepalive? or send periodic comment heartbeats from runtime to keep connection active so edge router doesn't consider idle. can we add 15s whitespace pings for streaming responses?
Keiko: runtime already supports heartbeat, but config defaults to 60s. if edge timeout is 30s, we need to lower default to 15s for hosted. I'll open a roll tomorrow.
Maya: for billing side, we need to avoid labeling these as 5xx for customers where client FIN occurs. ops: can billing pipeline check for downstream FIN before counting 5xx?
Raj: agreed — we can add a rule: if kernel logs indicate client RST/FIN within X seconds of last byte and upstream status==UPSTREAM_RESET, mark as client-abort and exclude from metered 5xx buckets. I'll draft a change.
Devon: also add an alert suppression rule so customers are not auto-escalated when this pattern occurs.
Maya: I'll reply to the customer: explain probable edge idle timeout, propose heartbeat change and bill adjustment while we investigate. draft: "We think an intermediate router is closing idle streaming connections. As a workaround, enable heartbeat/ping every 15s or upgrade to our dedicated session mode. We've flagged the billing entry and will refund miscounted 5xx while we deploy a fix."
Maya: cc @Keiko @Raj @Devon — please confirm ETA for infra fix and billing rule change so I can include in the message.
Keiko: infra rollout for heartbeat default change: 48h with canary tomorrow.
Raj: billing rule patch: 24h dev -> canary 6h -> prod 36h.
Devon: ops changes to alerting and docs update: 36h.
Maya: thanks team — I'll send the reply and create a support follow-up with refund request and link to the canary. action items: Keiko infra heartbeat default change (PR+canary), Raj billing classifier tweak, Devon alert suppression and docs, Maya customer comms. :thumbsup:
